players.product: NVLink Switch, B200 GPU, GB200 superchip

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FY2026 results (CFO Colette Kress): record revenue, 'Total revenue of $68 billion was up 73% year-over-year, accelerating from Q3.' Q4 data center revenue of $62 billion rose 75% year-over-year and 22% sequentially, 'driven primarily by sustained strength in Blackwell and the Blackwell Ultra ramp'; Grace Blackwell systems accounted for roughly 2/3 of data center revenue in the quarter; a record sequential add of $11 billion in data center revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $68 billion (+73% YoY); data center $62 billion (+75% YoY, +22% QoQ); Grace Blackwell roughly 2/3 of data center revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Blackwell installed base and generational leap: 'Today, nearly 9 gigawatts of infrastructure on Blackwell are deployed' at major CSPs, hyperscalers, AI model makers and enterprises, nearly a year after Grace Blackwell NVL72 systems were released. GB300 NVL72 achieved up to 50x performance per watt and 35x lower cost per token versus Hopper (InferenceX), and CUDA optimization delivered up to 5x better performance on GB200 NVL72 within 4 months. Demand so tight that 'even Hopper and much of the 6-year-old Ampere based products are sold out in the cloud'; Huang: even 6-year-old GPUs in the cloud 'are completely consumed and the pricing is going up.'
quarterly_data.figure: nearly 9 gigawatts of Blackwell deployed; up to 50x performance per watt and 35x lower cost per token vs Hopper

players.product: Vera Rubin platform (Rubin GPU, Vera CPU, NVLink switch, Spectrum-X / Quantum-X networking)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2027 outlook: revenue expected to be $78 billion, plus or minus 2%, with most growth from data center; no data center compute revenue from China assumed. GAAP / non-GAAP gross margins 74.9% / 75% (plus or minus 50 basis points), full-year gross margins still in the mid-70s while preparing for the Vera Rubin transition. Non-GAAP results now include stock-based compensation; Q1 GAAP / non-GAAP opex approximately $7.7 billion / $7.5 billion; full-year non-GAAP opex to grow in the low 40s year-over-year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 FY2027 revenue guide $78 billion, plus or minus 2%; non-GAAP gross margin 75%; full-year gross margins in the mid-70s

quarterly_data.signal: Demand visibility and supply: 'we expect sequential revenue growth throughout calendar 2026, exceeding what was included in the $500 billion Blackwell and Rubin revenue opportunity we shared last year.' NVIDIA believes it has 'inventory and supply commitments in place to address future demand, including shipments extending into calendar 2027.' Inventory grew 8% quarter-over-quarter and purchase commitments increased significantly — inventory and capacity secured 'to meet demand beyond the next several quarters', further out than usual; 'we expect tightness in the supply for our advanced architectures to persist.'
quarterly_data.figure: sequential revenue growth throughout calendar 2026, exceeding what was included in the $500 billion Blackwell and Rubin revenue opportunity; inventory grew 8% QoQ; supply commitments include shipments extending into calendar 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Rubin platform (unveiled at CES) comprises 6 new chips: Vera CPU, Rubin GPU, NVLink 6 Switch, ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, BlueField-4 DPUs and Spectrum-6 Ethernet switch; trains MOE models with 1/4 the number of GPUs and reduces inference token costs by up to 10x versus Blackwell. 'We shipped our first Vera Rubin samples to customers earlier this week, and we remain on track to commence production shipments in the second half of the year.' Modular cable-free tray design improves resiliency and serviceability relative to Blackwell. Kress: Blackwell will still be sold alongside Vera Rubin during the year; 'It's too early yet to determine how much' of the Vera Rubin ramp starts in the second half, but 'We do expect pretty much every single customer to be purchasing Vera Rubin.'
quarterly_data.figure: 6 new chips; 1/4 the GPUs for MOE training; up to 10x lower inference token cost vs Blackwell; first samples shipped, production shipments in second half

quarterly_data.signal: Groq inference technology (the transcript prints the name as 'Grok'): Huang — 'we recently entered into a nonexclusive licensing agreement with Grok for its low latency inference technology and welcome the team of brilliant engineers to NVIDIA. As we did with Mellanox, we will extend NVIDIA's architecture with Grok's innovations'; 'we'll extend our architecture with Grok as an accelerator', low latency decoder details to be shared at GTC.

Anthropic will train an inference on Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin system.' Later: Anthropic's revenue is about 10x in a year and they are 'severely capacity constrained because the demand is just incredible.'

players.product: H200/B200/GB200 GPU accelerators and HGX/GB200 NVL boards

quarterly_data.signal: China: 'While small amounts of H200 products for China-based customers were approved by the U.S. government, we have yet to generate any revenue. And we do not know whether any imports will be allowed into China.' Chinese competitors 'bolstered by recent IPOs are making progress'; the Q1 FY2027 outlook assumes no data center compute revenue from China.

contracts.signal: Huang: 'Last week, we announced that Meta is deploying millions of Blackwells and Rubin GPUs, NVIDIA CPUs and Spectrum x Ethernet for training and inference.' Kress: Meta Superintelligence Labs trains and deploys its frontier agentic AI systems on the same NVIDIA infrastructure.
contracts.units: millions of Blackwells and Rubin GPUs, plus NVIDIA CPUs and Spectrum-X Ethernet
contracts.date_signed: announced the week before the 02-25-2026 call

quarterly_data.signal: Standalone Vera CPU push (Huang): 'It's the only data center CPU that supports LPDDR5', designed for very high data processing and single-threaded performance; 'Vera was designed to be an excellent CPU for post-training' where AI agents learn to use tools that run in CPU-only or CPU-plus-GPU environments; Grace was built for single-threaded performance 'and Vera is off the charts better than that.' More detail promised at GTC.

players.product: NVLink Switch / Spectrum-X / Quantum InfiniBand fabric

quarterly_data.signal: Networking 'generating $11 billion in revenue, up more than 3.5x year-over-year'; scale-up and scale-out both grew double digits sequentially on NVLink, Spectrum-X Ethernet and InfiniBand; year-over-year growth driven primarily by NVLink 72 scale-up switches. 'In Q4, we announced that we will enable AWS with NVLink to integrate with their custom silicon.' Huang: 'Every rack comes with 9 nodes of switches. And each of them has 2 chips in it. And in the future, they'll have more'; NVIDIA is 'probably the largest Ethernet networking company in the world today', with Spectrum-X scale-across linking data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: networking $11 billion, up more than 3.5x YoY; 9 nodes of switches per rack, 2 chips each

players.product: GB200 / GB300 / Vera Rubin GPU systems

quarterly_data.signal: Customer mix: the top 5 cloud providers and hyperscalers 'collectively account for a little over 50% of our data center revenue'; analyst expectations for their 2026 CapEx are 'up nearly $120 billion since the start of the year and approaching $700 billion.' The rest (AI model makers, enterprises, supercomputing, sovereigns) is 'a very fast-growing area'. Sovereign AI business 'more than tripled year-over-year and over $30 billion' in fiscal 2026, driven primarily by customers in Canada, France, the Netherlands, Singapore and the U.K.
quarterly_data.figure: top 5 CSPs a little over 50% of data center revenue; sovereign AI over $30 billion in FY2026 (more than tripled)

quarterly_data.signal: Die architecture (Huang, answering a question on customized silicon): 'every time you cross a dilate, you have a dilate, you have to cross an interface. Every time you cross an interface, you add latency, you add power unnecessarily' (term as printed in the transcript); 'if you look at the Grace Blackwell architecture and the Rubin architecture, we use 2 giant reticle-limited dies', reducing interface crossings.
quarterly_data.figure: 2 giant reticle-limited dies (Grace Blackwell and Rubin)
